Match List - I with List - II.

List - I (Complex) List - II (Primary valency and Secondary valency)
(A) [Co(en)2Cl2]Cl (I) 3,    6
(B) [Pt(NH3)2Cl(NO2)] (II) 3,    4
(C) Hg [Co(SCN)4] (III) 2,    6
(D) [Mg (EDTA)]2− (IV) 2,    4

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
en.explanation:
Primary valency is the oxidation state of the central metal and secondary valency is its coordination number.

(A) : the complex ion is , so and Co is ; two bidentate en and two give coordination number 6, so (3, 6), which is (I).

(B) : , so Pt is ; four monodentate ligands give coordination number 4, so (2, 4), which is (IV).

(C) : the cation is , so the anion is and gives Co as ; four ligands give coordination number 4, so (2, 4), which is also (IV).

(D) : , so Mg is ; hexadentate EDTA gives coordination number 6, so (2, 6), which is (III).

The correct match is (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III), with (II) (3, 4) fitting no complex; no option gives this match, and option (C) differs only in pairing (C) with (II), which would require Co in the state, so this question is treated as a bonus.

en.content:
The correct statements from the following are :

(A) Tl3+ is a powerful oxidising agent

(B) Al3+ does not get reduced easily

(C) Both Al3+ and Tl3+ are very stable in solution

(D) Tl1+ is more stable than Tl3+

(E) Al3+ and Tl1+ are highly stable

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
en.explanation:
(i) True: Tl1+ is more stable than Tl3+ due to the inert pair effect. Therefore, Tl3+ acts as a powerful oxidizing agent.

(ii) True: The standard reduction potential for Al3+/Al is -1.66 V, indicating that Al3+ is difficult to reduce and thus highly stable.

(iii) False: Tl3+ is not stable in solution.

(iv) True: Tl1+ is more stable than Tl3+.

(v) True: Both Al3+ and Tl1+ are highly stable in their respective oxidation states.

en.content:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : On hydrolysis, oligo peptides give rise to fewer number of α-amino acids while proteins give rise to a large number of β-amino acids.

Statement (II) : Natural proteins are denatured by acids which convert the water soluble form of fibrous proteins to their water insoluble form.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.content: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

en.explanation:
When oligopeptides undergo hydrolysis, they yield a small number of α-amino acids. In contrast, proteins do not produce β-amino acids upon hydrolysis. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Furthermore, natural proteins, when subjected to denaturation by acids, do not convert fibrous proteins from a water-soluble to a water-insoluble form, as fibrous proteins are inherently not water-soluble. Therefore, Statement II is also incorrect.

In conclusion, both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

hi.explanation:

इसके अतिरिक्त, प्राकृतिक प्रोटीन, जब अम्लों द्वारा विकृतीकरण के अधीन किए जाते हैं, तो रेशेदार प्रोटीन को जल-विलेय से जल-अविलेय रूप में परिवर्तित नहीं करते हैं, क्योंकि रेशेदार प्रोटीन स्वाभाविक रूप से जल-विलेय नहीं होते हैं। इसलिए, कथन II भी गलत है।

निष्कर्ष में, कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

The descending order of basicity of the following amines is :

(D)

(E)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
en.explanation:
A is aniline, B is 4-methoxyaniline, C is 4-nitroaniline, D is methylamine and E is dimethylamine.

In alkylamines the nitrogen lone pair is localised and the alkyl groups release electrons to N (+I effect); in water the secondary amine is the stronger base, so (E, ) > (D, ).

In arylamines the lone pair is delocalised into the ring, so all three are much weaker bases than the alkylamines.

Among the arylamines, p- donates electrons into the ring (+R effect) and raises the electron density on N, so B () > A (); p- withdraws electrons (−R, −I) and delocalises the lone pair further, so C () is the weakest.

Order of basicity: E > D > B > A > C.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

ऐरिलऐमीनों में एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म वलय में विस्थानीकृत हो जाता है, इसलिए तीनों ऐल्किलऐमीनों की तुलना में बहुत दुर्बल क्षारक हैं।

ऐरिलऐमीनों में, p- वलय में इलेक्ट्रॉन देता है (+R प्रभाव) और N पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व बढ़ाता है, अतः B () > A (); p- इलेक्ट्रॉन खींचता है (−R, −I) और एकाकी युग्म को और अधिक विस्थानीकृत करता है, अतः C () सबसे दुर्बल है।

क्षारकता का क्रम : E > D > B > A > C।

अतः, सही विकल्प (C) है।

en.content: A mixture of 1 g each of chlorobenzene, aniline, and benzoic acid is dissolved in 50 mL ethyl acetate and placed in a separating funnel. 5 M NaOH (30 mL) was added in the same funnel. The funnel was shaken vigorously and then kept aside. The ethyl acetate layer in the funnel contains :
en.explanation:
Benzoic acid is a carboxylic acid, so aqueous NaOH converts it into sodium benzoate, an ionic salt that dissolves in the aqueous layer and leaves the ethyl acetate layer:

Chlorobenzene (neutral; its aryl bond is not attacked by aqueous NaOH under these conditions) and aniline (a base) do not react with NaOH, so both remain dissolved in ethyl acetate.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

Statement I: in a cis-1,2-dihaloethene both C–X bond dipoles point to the same side of the double bond, so their resultant is not zero. Cl is more electronegative than Br, so the C–Cl bond dipoles are larger and cis-1,2-dichloroethene is more polar than cis-1,2-dibromoethene. Statement I is correct.

Statement II: in trans-1,2-dibromoethene the two C–Br bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel, so , whereas cis-1,2-dibromoethene has .

The weaker dipole–dipole attraction gives the trans isomer the lower boiling point, so the first part of Statement II is true, but the trans isomer is less polar than the cis isomer, not more polar. Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

Given below are two statements :

1 M aqueous solutions of each of Cu(NO3)2, AgNO3, Hg2(NO3)2, Mg(NO3)2 are electrolysed using inert electrodes. Given: E0Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E0Hg22+/Hg = 0.79 V, E0Cu2+/Cu = 0.24 V and E0Mg2+/Mg = -2.37 V.

Statement (I) : With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu.

Statement (II) : Magnesium will not be deposited at the cathode instead oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

en.explanation:
Let’s analyze the situation step by step.

We have 1 M aqueous solutions of:

with

with

with

with

In an electrolytic cell with inert electrodes, reduction occurs at the cathode. The ion with the highest (most positive) reduction potential will be reduced (or deposited) first. Therefore, as we increase the applied voltage (making the cathode sufficiently negative), the metals will begin to deposit in the order of their reduction potentials.

The order of reduction (deposition) will be:

First, silver ()

Next, mercury ()

Then, copper ()

So, Statement (I) which says “With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu” is correct.

For magnesium, the reduction potential is very negative (). In aqueous solution, before reaching such a negative potential, water will be reduced. The cathodic reaction for water typically is:

which leads to the evolution of hydrogen gas, not oxygen. (Oxygen is produced at the anode during the oxidation of water.)

Hence, Statement (II) erroneously states that “oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode” when in fact, if magnesium were to be reduced (which it won’t be), water reduction would yield hydrogen gas. Thus, Statement (II) is incorrect.

Summary:

Statement (I) is correct.

Statement (II) is incorrect.

Therefore, the most appropriate answer is:

Option C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

en.explanation:
A half-filled subshell (, , ) has one electron in each degenerate orbital, all with parallel spins; this symmetrical distribution of electrons gives extra stability, so (A) is correct.

With one electron per orbital, no two electrons are paired in the same orbital, so the coulombic repulsion energy is smaller; (B) is correct.

Electrons with parallel spins in degenerate orbitals can exchange their positions, and the number of such exchanges is maximum in a half-filled subshell, so the exchange energy released is larger; (D) is correct.

Electrons of the same subshell shield one another relatively poorly, so each experiences a higher effective nuclear charge; (E) is correct.

Exchange stabilisation arises from parallel-spin electrons in degenerate orbitals (equal-energy orbitals of one subshell), not in non-degenerate orbitals, so (C) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

अर्ध पूरित उपकोश (, , ) के प्रत्येक समभ्रंश कक्षक में एक इलेक्ट्रॉन होता है और सभी के चक्रण समांतर होते हैं; इलेक्ट्रॉनों का यह सममित वितरण अतिरिक्त स्थायित्व देता है, अतः (A) सही है।

एक ही उपकोश के इलेक्ट्रॉन एक-दूसरे को अपेक्षाकृत कम परिरक्षित करते हैं, इसलिए प्रत्येक पर उच्चतर प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश कार्य करता है; (E) सही है।

विनिमय स्थायित्व समभ्रंश कक्षकों (एक उपकोश के समान ऊर्जा वाले कक्षकों) में समांतर चक्रण वाले इलेक्ट्रॉनों से उत्पन्न होता है, असमभ्रंश कक्षकों में नहीं, अतः (C) गलत है।

en.content: Which one of the following forces cannot be expressed in terms of potential energy?
en.explanation:
The correct answer is:

Option A: Frictional force

Here's why:

Conservative vs. Non-Conservative Forces:

Conservative Forces: These are forces for which the work done is independent of the path taken; they only depend on the initial and final positions. For conservative forces, you can define a potential energy function. Examples include Coulomb’s force, gravitational force, and the restoring force of a spring.

Non-Conservative Forces: These forces depend on the path taken and usually result in energy dissipation (often as heat). Friction is a typical example, and hence, it cannot be described solely by a potential energy function.

Example Explanations:

Coulomb’s Force: It is a conservative force because the work done in moving a charge in an electric field only depends on the difference in electric potential between two points.

Gravitational Force: It is also conservative. The potential energy associated with gravitational force is given by gravitational potential energy, for example, near the Earth’s surface.

Restoring Force: For a spring, the force is given by Hooke’s law: and the corresponding potential energy is This is a conservative force.

Since friction is a non-conservative force that dissipates energy, it cannot be expressed in terms of potential energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A: Frictional force.

hi.content: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा बल, स्थितिज ऊर्जा के पदों में व्यक्त नहीं किया जा सकता है ?
hi.explanation:
सही उत्तर है:

विकल्प A: घर्षण बल

यहाँ कारण है:

संरक्षी बनाम असंरक्षी बल:

संरक्षी बल: ये वे बल हैं जिनके लिए किया गया कार्य अपनाए गए पथ से स्वतंत्र होता है; वे केवल प्रारंभिक और अंतिम स्थितियों पर निर्भर करते हैं। संरक्षी बलों के लिए, आप एक स्थितिज ऊर्जा फलन परिभाषित कर सकते हैं। उदाहरणों में कूलॉम बल, गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल, और स्प्रिंग का प्रत्यानयन बल शामिल हैं।

असंरक्षी बल: ये बल अपनाए गए पथ पर निर्भर करते हैं और आमतौर पर ऊर्जा अपव्यय (प्रायः ऊष्मा के रूप में) में परिणत होते हैं। घर्षण बल एक विशिष्ट उदाहरण है, और इसलिए, इसे केवल स्थितिज ऊर्जा फलन द्वारा वर्णित नहीं किया जा सकता।

उदाहरण स्पष्टीकरण:

कूलॉम बल: यह एक संरक्षी बल है क्योंकि विद्युत क्षेत्र में आवेश को स्थानांतरित करने में किया गया कार्य केवल दो बिंदुओं के बीच विद्युत विभव के अंतर पर निर्भर करता है।

गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल: यह भी संरक्षी है। गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल से संबद्ध स्थितिज ऊर्जा गुरुत्वीय स्थितिज ऊर्जा द्वारा दी जाती है, उदाहरण के लिए, पृथ्वी की सतह के निकट ।

प्रत्यानयन बल: स्प्रिंग के लिए, बल हुक के नियम द्वारा दिया जाता है: और संगत स्थितिज ऊर्जा है। यह एक संरक्षी बल है।

चूंकि घर्षण बल एक असंरक्षी बल है जो ऊर्जा को अपव्ययित करता है, इसे स्थितिज ऊर्जा के रूप में व्यक्त नहीं किया जा सकता।

इसलिए, सही उत्तर है विकल्प A: घर्षण बल।

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The outer body of an aircraft is made of metal which protects persons sitting inside from lightning strikes.

Reason (R) : The electric field inside the cavity enclosed by a conductor is zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.content: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

en.explanation:
The assertion suggests that the outer body of an aircraft is made of metal to protect passengers from lightning strikes. The reason provided is that the electric field inside a cavity enclosed by a conductor is zero.

This reasoning is based on the property of metallic conductors, where the electric field within a conductor's cavity is indeed zero. This phenomenon occurs because the charges on a conductor redistribute themselves to cancel any external electric fields within the conductor. Thus, if lightning were to strike an aircraft, the metal body would direct the electric charges along its surface, effectively shielding the interior where passengers are located.

Therefore, the assertion and the reason are both correct, and the reason correctly explains why the metal body of an aircraft shields passengers from lightning. This aligns with the principles of electromagnetic shielding. The key point is that the conductive nature of the aircraft’s metal body ensures no electric field permeates the interior, keeping passengers safe.

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Magnetic monopoles do not exist.

Reason (R): Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.content: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

en.explanation:
The assertion states that magnetic monopoles do not exist. This is consistent with current experimental findings and the standard formulation of Maxwell's equations.

The reason provided is that magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops. This is mathematically expressed by the Maxwell equation:

This equation tells us that there are no "sources" or "sinks" of magnetic fields (unlike electric fields, which can originate or terminate at charges). In other words, magnetic field lines neither begin nor end; they loop continuously.

Since the fact that the magnetic field lines form closed loops is a direct consequence of the absence of isolated magnetic charges (monopoles), the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

The most appropriate answer is Option A.
